chief_complaint: progressive headache, cognitive changes, and right-sided weakness
hpi_details: A 38-year-old female presents to the clinic with progressive headache, cognitive changes, and right-sided weakness. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she suffered a mini-stroke or a severe complicated migraine like the ones her mother used to experience.
concerns: She is worried that she is becoming permanently paralyzed and will no longer be able to lift and care for her young children.
expectations: She hopes to get an MRI of her brain today to see what is causing the right-sided heaviness and weakness.

history.answer: My head has been hurting more and more over the past month, and recently my right arm and leg have become weak and clumsy.
It started gradually about four weeks ago as a mild ache, but it has grown steadily more intense and persistent every week.
At first it came and went a few times a week, but over the last ten days the headache has been present almost continuously throughout the day.
The pain is mostly deep inside the left side of my head and around my left temple, though sometimes the whole head feels heavy.
It feels like a deep, persistent aching pressure, and right now I would rate it around a six or seven out of ten.
It is noticeably worse in the morning right when I wake up, and on several occasions the throbbing has woken me up before my alarm.
Bending over to pick things up or coughing makes the pressure inside my head throb much worse, whereas resting quietly with my head elevated eases it slightly.
I have felt queasy and nauseated in the mornings over the past week, but I have not actually vomited.
I haven't had flashing zig-zag lights or vision loss before the headache starts, but my sight feels slightly blurry when the pressure gets intense. Bright light doesn't bother me particularly.
My husband noticed that I have been forgetting simple everyday words, taking much longer to finish work spreadsheets, and having trouble concentrating.
Over the past two weeks my right hand has become weak so I keep dropping pens, and my right foot drags slightly when I walk.
My right arm and leg feel somewhat clumsy and slightly tingly at times, but not completely numb.
I struggle to retrieve the right words when speaking, but my family says my pronunciation is not completely slurred.
No, I have not had any convulsions, muscle jerking, staring spells, or loss of consciousness.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, neck stiffness, or skin rashes.
I have not had any head trauma, falls, or accidents recently.
No, I have not noticed any eye redness, tearing, runny nose, or drooping of my eyelids.
I tried taking acetaminophen a few times last week, but it barely made any difference, so I stopped taking it.
No one else in my home has headaches, and we do not use kerosene or gas heaters.
I have never been diagnosed with high blood pressure, diabetes, heart conditions, or cancer.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I am not taking any prescription medications, birth control pills, or over-the-counter supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or environmental triggers.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine on social occasions, perhaps once or twice a month.
I work as an office accountant and live with my husband and our ten-year-old daughter.
Both of my parents are alive and well in their sixties, and no one in my family has had brain tumors or neurological illnesses.
My last period was two weeks ago and my cycles are regular every twenty-eight days. We use barrier contraception, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

I thought maybe I had a mini-stroke or an unusual migraine, since my mother used to get migraines that made her limbs go numb. I'm terrified that this weakness means I'm becoming paralyzed and won't be able to hold or look after my young kids.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/80 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert and oriented to person, place, and time, but demonstrates mild psychomotor slowing and slight word-finding hesitation.
Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light; funduscopy reveals bilateral optic disc swelling consistent with papilledema, without retinal hemorrhages.
Mild right central facial droop with forehead movement spared; extraocular muscles intact without nystagmus; remaining cranial nerves intact.
Pronator drift present on the right; muscle strength is grade 4/5 in the right upper and lower extremities, and grade 5/5 throughout the left side.
Hyperreflexia (3+) in the right biceps, patellar, and Achilles tendons; positive Babinski sign on the right; normal 2+ reflexes and flexor plantar response on the left.
Mildly decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick over the right arm and leg; intact sensation on the left side.
Mildly unsteady gait with slight circumduction of the right leg; finger-to-nose and rapid alternating movements show mild clumsiness on the right side due to motor weakness; negative Romberg test.
Supple neck with full active and passive range of motion; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
No tenderness over the frontal or maxillary sinuses, and no tenderness or thickening over either temporal artery.
